# Attest (Attest.NET)

> Generates property-based tests for changed code, then refutes each candidate before delivery: properties that fail on the current (working) code are rejected as wrong; properties that survive mutations of the changed lines are rejected as trivial. Only properties that are true AND kill at least one mutant are delivered; each shipped with the mutant it killed as evidence, re-verified at report time. The LLM proposes; the machine refutes. A deterministic secret Sanitizer runs before any code reaches an LLM, and again before the report renders.

Unlike example-test generators (Copilot, Qodo, Cover-Agent) and unlike Meta's internal ACH system, Attest generates properties (invariants) rather than example tests, targets .NET, and never uses an LLM to judge, classify or verify anything.

Note: search for "Attest.NET"; an unrelated `Attest.*` fakes-framework family exists on NuGet.

- Package: `Attest.NET` (library), `Attest.Cli` (dotnet tool)
- Targets: `net8.0`, `net10.0`
- Stack: FsCheck v3 + xUnit + Stryker.NET
- LLM: Anthropic, Ollama (fully local), or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; bring your own key
- License: MIT
- Status: in development

## Install

```bash
dotnet tool install -g Attest.Cli
```

## Primary usage

```bash
# first run in a new repo: generates attest.json interactively
attest init

# check the environment before anything costs money or CI minutes
attest doctor

# propose, validate, falsify and report for the current diff against main
attest --diff origin/main --project path/to/YourProject.csproj

# optionally scope git operations to a different repository root
attest --diff origin/main --project path/to/YourProject.csproj --repo path/to/repo
```

`--diff` and `--project` are both required; `--repo` defaults to the current directory. No other flags are parsed today: `--dry-run`, `--max-llm-cost`, `--air-gapped`, `--trace-id`, `--format` do not exist yet. `--max-llm-cost`, `--trace-id` and `--format` (JSON/SARIF output) are on the v1.x roadmap; `--dry-run` and `--air-gapped` are not currently planned. The mutant ceiling is set via `attest.json`'s `maxMutants` field, not a flag.

Output today is a plain-text funnel report to stdout: delivered properties (each with the killed mutant as evidence), rejected candidates (reason `Wrong` or `Trivial` for a verdict on the candidate itself, plus a handful of narrower named reasons — synthesis failure, a tooling crash mid-run, exceeding the mutant ceiling — that are not a verdict on the candidate at all), and quarantined candidates (nondeterministic under repeated seeded runs; often a real finding about the code under test). The funnel renders all stage counts even when zero properties are delivered, so "nothing testable in this diff" is distinguishable from "the tool failed". Structured (`--format json`) and SARIF/markdown output are roadmap, not built.

## CI usage

Not yet published: a GitHub Action (`danellalc/Attest.NET@v1`) with fork-PR and fetch-depth guidance is v1 scope but not built. Until then, call the CLI directly as a step:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0   # REQUIRED: shallow checkout breaks --diff silently
- run: dotnet tool install -g Attest.Cli
- run: attest --diff origin/main --project path/to/YourProject.csproj
  env:
    ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
```

Known limitation: secrets are not available to fork PRs on GitHub. For public repos, run Attest on pushes to main branches, or point a fork-PR run at Ollama instead. A `--fail-on-secret` gate and PR comments that edit themselves in place on subsequent pushes are both roadmap, not implemented: the Sanitizer redacts unconditionally today, and there is no PR-comment-posting mechanism yet.

## Configuration

`attest.json` at repo root (`provider` and `model` are required; `maxMutants` is optional, default 200):

```json
{
  "provider": "anthropic",
  "model": "claude-sonnet-5",
  "maxMutants": 200
}
```

`provider` is `"anthropic"`, `"ollama"`, or `"openai-compatible"`. The third one reaches any backend speaking the OpenAI Chat Completions API shape (OpenAI, Groq, DeepSeek, Together, a self-hosted vLLM/llama.cpp server) and needs two more fields:

```json
{
  "provider": "openai-compatible",
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "baseUrl": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
  "jsonMode": "object",
  "inputPricePerMillion": 0.15,
  "outputPricePerMillion": 0.60
}
```

`baseUrl` is required for `openai-compatible`; the API key comes from the `LLM_API_KEY` environment variable (not `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, which is Anthropic-only). `jsonMode` (`"schema"` / `"object"` / `"none"`, default `"object"`) controls how hard the response is constrained to JSON -- not every backend supports `"schema"` (full structured output), so this is config, not auto-detected, and there is no automatic fallback (the design forbids retry loops: a backend that rejects the configured mode fails the call, not a second request with a different one). `inputPricePerMillion`/`outputPricePerMillion` are optional; without both, the report shows LLM cost as not tracked rather than guessing or showing a misleading `$0.00`.

Run `attest init` to generate this file interactively instead of writing it by hand. `maxLlmCost`, `failOnSecret`, `quarantineRetries` and `webhookUrl` are not real fields today — a per-run cost ceiling, secret-scan gating and webhook notifications are all v1.x/roadmap; passing them is silently ignored, not an error.

Custom generators for domain types (private constructors, EF entities) are v1 design scope — the escape hatch the Synthesizer needs to survive real domain types — but are not implemented yet. There is no `examples/` folder in the repo today.

## Key guarantees

- No source code reaches the network without passing the deterministic secret Sanitizer; the report passes through it again before rendering.
- No property reaches the user without killing at least one mutant, re-verified at report time.
- The LLM is used only to propose. Validation, falsification and equivalence handling are deterministic: no LLM judging (Meta's ACH does this at 47% recall; Attest refuses the pattern).
- Mutation runs only on changed lines. The mutant count Stryker reports is verified against the expected count; a mismatch aborts loudly instead of silently mutating the whole project.
- Same diff, same seed, same cached proposals = byte-identical report.
- Ollama = fully local: set `"provider": "ollama"` in `attest.json` and no call ever reaches a hosted provider.

## Common mistakes when using this tool

- Do not skip `attest doctor` in a new environment: it catches shallow git clones and, for Ollama, a configured model that hasn't been pulled — before they cost money or CI minutes. It does not check Docker (`attest --diff` never uses it) and cannot check Anthropic model deprecation without spending an API call; for Anthropic it only confirms the API key is set.
- Do not run on the whole repository: it is diff-scoped by design. Use `--diff` against a base ref, with full git history available.
- Do not treat delivered properties as proof of intent. They prove tests detect change; the oracle problem is structural. Read the plain-language rendering of each property.
- Do not skip quarantined results: quarantine usually means the code under test is nondeterministic, which is a finding.
- Do not disable the Sanitizer or the falsification stage. Each one exists because of a specific documented failure mode (public secret leaks; false-green tests).
- If synthesis fails on a domain type today, that is a real `Unsynthesizable` rejection, not a bug to work around by excluding the file; a custom-generator escape hatch is v1 scope but not built yet.

## Not supported

- Languages other than .NET (TypeScript and Python adapters are roadmap; the adapter contract will be public).
- Whole-system correctness proving (see Antithesis).
- UI / E2E / browser testing.
- LLM-based verification of anything.
- IDE extensions, hosted dashboards, compliance report generation.
